mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.75% over three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds the risk-free rate by more than 200 basis points.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate above 5.5% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5.5% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in triggered episodes, or the median return is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags down the S&P 500, producing negative returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above 3% within the same month signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and increases discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > previous month + 0.5% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the average return is not statistically below the long-run mean at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the previous six-month average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market sentiment, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST exceeds six-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in triggered episodes, or the median return is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month is a contradictory signal indicating data inconsistency or sectoral shifts; under such conditions, S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days exhibit no predictable direction and should be treated as noise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE also increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are significantly positive or negative in more than 55% of triggered months at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) for four consecutive months signals a buildup of household savings that has not yet translated into consumption, suggesting future demand may remain weak; this dynamic is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below zero at 95% confidence.
